data.title: Lost Astronaut 2: Broken Transmitter
data.statement:
This is part 2 of the Lost Astronaut series. Part 1: <<Lost Astronaut>> (Medium).

Thanks to your program, Earth decoded the astronaut's first signals

But his space-made transmitter, built from broken spaceship parts, is getting worse. It still converts each character randomly to <<binary>>, <<octal>>, <<hexadecimal>>, or leaves it <<as it is>>. Now it has also stopped sending the separators between values, so every signal arrives as one long stream of symbols.

Luckily, the astronaut expected this. Before each message, he now sends two numbers:
[[N]]: how many characters his message has
[[CHECKSUM]]: the sum of the ASCII codes of all characters in his message

Each character of the message is sent in exactly one of these forms:
binary, for example {{1101111}} for {{o}}
octal, for example {{157}} for {{o}}
hexadecimal with lowercase digits, for example {{6f}} for {{o}}
the character itself, for example {{o}}

Numbers never have leading zeros. The message contains only <<letters and spaces>>, so any value that decodes to something else is not a valid reading.

A stream can often be read in more than one way. For example, {{m11011111576e}} can be read as:
{{m}} {{1101111}} {{157}} {{6e}} = {{moon}} (4 characters)
{{m}} {{110}} {{111}} {{115}} {{76}} {{e}} = {{mHIMve}} (6 characters)

Only one reading has exactly [[N]] characters <<and>> matches [[CHECKSUM]]. That reading is the astronaut's message.

Mission control needs you to rebuild the original message. Good luck!

testCases.title: 10th Signal
testCases.testOut: I am on the ship Thank you all for not giving up on me We took off right on time but a solar flare fried the navigation computer and now the pilot has no idea where we are The engine works and we have fuel so we are not lost yet just confused Please help us find the way home We will send our position every hour

testCases.title: Validator 7
testCases.testOut: Welcome aboard We are so happy to hear from you again Your family was in the control room when you took off and nobody could stop smiling Do not fire the engine until we find a safe route Send your position every hour and we will guide you home step by step Hang in there you are almost home and we will be waiting for you

lastVersion.statementHTML:
Goal

This is part 2 of the Lost Astronaut series. Part 1: Lost Astronaut (Medium).

Thanks to your program, Earth decoded the astronaut's first signals

But his space-made transmitter, built from broken spaceship parts, is getting worse. It still converts each character randomly to binary, octal, hexadecimal, or leaves it as it is. Now it has also stopped sending the separators between values, so every signal arrives as one long stream of symbols.

Luckily, the astronaut expected this. Before each message, he now sends two numbers:
N: how many characters his message has
CHECKSUM: the sum of the ASCII codes of all characters in his message

Each character of the message is sent in exactly one of these forms:
binary, for example 1101111 for o
octal, for example 157 for o
hexadecimal with lowercase digits, for example 6f for o
the character itself, for example o

Numbers never have leading zeros. The message contains only letters and spaces, so any value that decodes to something else is not a valid reading.

A stream can often be read in more than one way. For example, m11011111576e can be read as:
m 1101111 157 6e = moon (4 characters)
m 110 111 115 76 e = mHIMve (6 characters)

Only one reading has exactly N characters and matches CHECKSUM. That reading is the astronaut's message.

Mission control needs you to rebuild the original message. Good luck!
Input
Line 1: an integer N, the number of characters in the original message
Line 2: an integer CHECKSUM, the sum of the ASCII codes of the original message
Line 3: a string STREAM, the received transmission. It may contain spaces, so read the whole line.
Output
The original message typed by the astronaut.
Constraints
2 ≤ N ≤ 350
1 ≤ length of STREAM ≤ 2450
The message contains only A to Z, a to z, and space ( ), and does not start or end with a space.
There is exactly one valid message.
Example
Input
11
1032
100100014511011001101100110111140100010111000011110010111010068
Output
Hello Earth
